article_info.title: OpenAI unveils Dots, an always-on AI agent, at DevDay 2026
article_info.summary: Powered by GPT-6 Astra, each Dot gets its own cloud computer and can connect to over 4,000 apps to handle tasks around the clock.
article_info.bullet_summary:
- **OpenAI** launched **Dots** on Tuesday at DevDay 2026, introducing always-on AI agents that learn user preferences and work proactively across projects.[1]
- Dots roll out to Pro and Business Premium users, alongside a new **$500/month** subscription tier with higher usage limits and faster speeds.[2]
- The launch intensifies competition with **Meta** [Meta Platforms, Inc.](pplx://entity_chip/0a07a0f4) **Muse** and comes a day after OpenAI scrapped its GPT-6.1 release over safety concerns.[2][3]

{"answer": "The launch arrives at a complicated moment for OpenAI. The day before DevDay, the company scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra after the model failed internal safety evaluations, with OpenAI's head of safety systems citing concerns about how the model "did not meet the bar for scope and authorization". Anthropic, meanwhile, released its Claude Opus 5.5 model last week, which outperformed GPT-6 Astra on most benchmarks.[1][2]

On the consumer side, Meta's Muse agent has been breaking adoption records. OpenAI countered with its own momentum figures, saying ChatGPT now reaches more than 1.2 billion weekly users.
